generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Sample from a small pool of realistic short strings; 5% of rows get a near-variant (case change, trailing space, or one-character edit) of a pool value; NULL only where nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_long: Sample from a pool of realistic sentences; 5% near-variants; NULL only where nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.integer: Sample uniformly from the stated range; include boundary values and one step on each side; NULL only where nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.real: Sample uniformly from the stated range with one decimal; include boundary values; NULL only where nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.date_iso: Sample a date in %Y-%m-%d format within the stated range; include boundary dates and one day on each side; NULL only where nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.enum: Sample uniformly from the listed values; 5% near-variants (case change) where the column is free text; NULL only where nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.flag: Sample from the listed flag values; NULL only where nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_share: 0.15 of text values are fresh (not reused from the pool) to create near-duplicates and unmatched joins.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share_default: Use the compact database null rate for the column, at least one NULL row per nullable column; plant NULLs in nullable foreign keys too.
generic_sampling_rules.fk_integrity: Every non-NULL foreign-key value must be drawn from the final surviving parent key set after PK/unique dedup and after compact+generated merge; validate references before insert and never emit a dangling FK.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_survival: Apply duplicate and tie injection before boundary injection, or exclude boundary rows from overwrite, so every specified boundary value is present in each instance.
generic_sampling_rules.tie_planting: For ORDER columns with tie_at_rank targets, deterministically set the two extreme rows to the same min and the two to the same max after boundary injection.
generic_sampling_rules.min_rows: Each table has at least as many rows as the largest boundary list for its columns; cycle boundaries across rows so all are present.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows every nullable column with 'generated rows: NULL 0 / n' (e.g. Person.birthdate 0/209, Award.person 0/76, Credit.person 0/623, Vote.stars 0/586, Award.season 0/76, Award.song 0/76). The specification's null_targets list and null_shares (e.g. Person.birthdate 0.642, Award.role 0.707, Award.season 1.0) require NULLs to be planted. In instance.py, _plant_nulls is only called for columns where null_share(spec, t, cm.name, 0.0) > 0.0, but the loaded specification (specification.json / _DEFAULT) is keyed under 'null_shares' with per-table dicts; the sampler path also drops None elements in ColumnSampler.__init__ ('self.elements = [e for e in elements if e is not None]'), and _init_sampler builds elements from original_values which include None but are filtered. More importantly, the FK columns (Award.person, Award.episode_id, Credit.person, Credit.episode_id, Vote.episode_id) are filled by fill_foreign_keys_consistently which filters out None ('pv = [v for v in pv if v is not None]') and never plants NULLs, contradicting the spec's nullable FK targets and the interface NULL rule. The result is zero NULLs in every nullable column across all 20 instances.
issues.requested_revision: Plant NULLs for every nullable column including nullable foreign keys: in fill_foreign_keys_consistently, after drawing parent values, apply _plant_nulls with the column's null_share (and at least one NULL row) for nullable FK columns; ensure _plant_nulls is actually reached for all nullable non-FK columns (verify null_share lookup against the loaded spec keys, and that the sampler does not strip the planted NULLs). Confirm execution feedback shows non-zero NULL counts matching the compact shares for Person.birthdate, Award.person, Award.role, Award.season, Award.song, Credit.person, Credit.episode_id, Vote.episode_id, Vote.stars, etc.

issues.evidence: specification.py _DEFAULT and the per-column exceptions specify boundary values that violate the semantic formulas, e.g. Episode.rating boundaries [4.9,5,5.1,9.9,10,10.1] with formula 'rating BETWEEN 0 AND 10'; Episode.votes boundaries [-1,0,1,4,5,6] with 'votes >= 0'; Episode.episode boundaries [0,1,2,4,5,6] with 'episode > 0'; Vote.stars boundaries [4..9] with 'stars BETWEEN 1 AND 10'. In instance.py, _enforce_formula clamps domain values but the boundary values are injected by NumberSampler.sample() (15% chance) and then clamped by _enforce_formula only if a 'domain' is present in the column spec. For Episode.rating the spec has domain [0.0,10.0] so 10.1 is clamped to 10.0 and -1 to 0 — this silently removes the intended boundary separation (the atomic summary explicitly wants values one step outside the range to test boundary predicates). The clamping makes the boundary values unreachable, so the comparison_boundary pattern for these columns cannot be exercised as specified.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile the boundary targets with the semantic formulas: either (a) drop out-of-range boundary values from the spec (keep only in-range boundaries plus the exact endpoints), or (b) if out-of-range values are intended to test boundary predicates, remove the corresponding formula clamp for those columns and document that the formula is a soft rule. As written, the spec and the formula enforcement contradict each other and the boundary values are never generated.

issues.evidence: The atomic summary lists comparison_boundary targets for Award.year as date-like strings ('2008-12-31','2009-01-01','2009-12-31','2010-01-01') and the spec's per_column_exceptions repeats these for Award.year, but Award.year is declared INTEGER and the semantic rule is 'year BETWEEN 1990 AND 2030'. The specification's own 'uncertainty' note acknowledges this ('treat as integer year'). The _DEFAULT spec correctly uses integer boundaries [2008,2009,2010,2017,2018], but the per_column_exceptions in the generation specification still carry the string targets, which cannot be generated into an INTEGER column.
issues.requested_revision: Designer should correct the Award.year comparison_boundary targets to integer years consistent with the INTEGER type and the 1990-2030 formula (e.g. 2008, 2009, 2010), removing the date-string targets that cannot be stored in an INTEGER column.

issues.evidence: The spec's semantic rule 'Episode.episode > 0' and 'Episode.votes >= 0' conflict with the boundary targets [0,1,2,4,5,6] for episode and [-1,0,1,4,5,6] for votes. issues.evidence: The spec's generic_sampling_rules state '5% of rows get a near-variant (case change, trailing space, or one-character edit)' and 'fresh_share 0.15 of text values are fresh'. In values.py StringSampler.sample, near-variants are applied with probability 0.5 (not 5%) and the mutation is a random append/prepend/truncate, not a case change or trailing space. EnumSampler applies case variants at 5% (correct), but StringSampler (used for Episode.title, Person.name, Credit.role, etc.) over-applies mutations at 50%, which will over-produce near-duplicates and unmatched joins beyond the specified share.
issues.requested_revision: Align StringSampler near-variant probability with the spec (5%) and implement the specified variant kinds (case change, trailing space, one-character edit) rather than the current 50% random append/truncate. Verify the fresh_share 0.15 is honored.

issues.evidence: The spec's dependencies list nullable FK children (Award.person, Award.episode_id, Credit.person, Credit.episode_id, Vote.episode_id) and the interface NULL rule requires NULL and non-NULL rows for nullable FKs. fill_foreign_keys_consistently always draws a non-NULL parent value when the parent has values ('out[cm.name] = [rng.choice(pv) for _ in range(n)] if pv else [None] * n'), so nullable FKs never receive NULLs. issues.evidence: Execution feedback reports fk_violations: 91 and validity.reasons.new_integrity_failures: 20 (all 20 instances invalid). The writer disables FK enforcement (`con.execute('pragma foreign_keys = OFF')` in writer.py) and appends rows without validating references, so generated child rows (Award.person/episode_id, Credit.person/episode_id, Vote.episode_id, Character_Award.award_id) can reference parent keys that were dropped by `sample_fresh_primary_keys`/`drop_unique_duplicates` or that never existed. The spec's `dependencies` require FK children to reference existing parent values.
issues.requested_revision: Ensure generated FK values are drawn only from the final surviving parent key set (after PK/unique dedup and after compact+generated merge), and re-enable/verify FK integrity (or validate references before insert). The instance must not introduce new FK violations relative to the compact database.

issues.evidence: instance.py `fill_foreign_keys_consistently` draws FK values from `compact + instance[pt][pc]` at the time the child table is built, but parent tables are later filtered by `sample_fresh_primary_keys` and `drop_unique_duplicates` (and self-FK remapping only handles `pt == t`). Rows dropped from the parent leave dangling child references. This is the direct cause of the 91 FK violations.
issues.requested_revision: Build parent tables fully (including dedup/filtering) before sampling child FKs, or post-process child FK columns to remap any value not present in the final parent key set to a valid parent value (or NULL where nullable).

issues.evidence: instance.py tie-planting block: `if (t, cm.name) in {('Episode','votes'),('Episode','rating')}: pass` is a no-op inside the loop; ties are only planted afterward via `_plant_ties`, which copies one random value onto another row. This does not guarantee a tie at rank 1 in both ASC and DESC directions as the spec's `ties_for_order_limit` targets require, and `_plant_ties` may overwrite a boundary value injected earlier.
issues.requested_revision: Implement deterministic rank-1 tie planting for Episode.votes and Episode.rating (e.g. set the two extreme rows to the same min and the two to the same max) after boundary injection, and remove the dead `pass` branch.

issues.evidence: `_inject_boundaries` places boundary values at the first rows, but subsequent `_inject_duplicates` (20-50% share) and `_plant_ties` overwrite arbitrary rows including those first rows, so guaranteed boundary presence is not actually guaranteed. Also `_inject_duplicates` picks a random source value that may itself be a boundary, spreading it widely and distorting the intended boundary distribution.
issues.requested_revision: Apply duplicate/tie injection before boundary injection, or exclude boundary rows from overwrite, so that every specified boundary value is present in each instance.

issues.evidence: Specification `semantic_rules_and_formulas` lists `Award.year BETWEEN 1990 AND 2030` and `Vote.stars BETWEEN 1 AND 10` etc. as formulas, but `hard_formulas` only contains `Award.result` and `Credit.credited`. The `Award.year` comparison_boundary targets are integers 2008/2009/2010 while the atomic-operation evidence shows `SUBSTRING(award.year,1,4)=2009` with date-like values ('2008-12-31' etc.), indicating the column may hold dates in the source. The spec's `uncertainty` note acknowledges this but the domain [1990,2030] is asserted without direct row evidence for Award.year values.
issues.requested_revision: Confirm Award.year's actual stored type/values from the compact database and align the domain and boundary targets (integer years vs. date strings) accordingly; document the evidence.

issues.evidence: Specification `null_targets` omits several nullable columns that the execution feedback shows as nullable (e.g. Award.award, Award.award_category, Award.organization, Award.result, Award.year, Character_Award.award_id, Character_Award.character, Credit.category, Credit.credited, Credit.role, Episode.air_date, Episode.episode, Episode.episode_image, Episode.number_in_series, Episode.rating, Episode.season, Episode.summary, Episode.title, Episode.votes, Vote.percent, Vote.votes). The NULL rule requires NULL and non-NULL rows for every nullable column; these columns show 'NULL 0 / n'.
issues.requested_revision: Extend `null_targets` (and `null_shares`) to cover every nullable column so the NULL rule is applied uniformly, or explicitly justify why these are treated as non-nullable.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows many nullable columns with 'generated rows: NULL 0 / n' (e.g. Episode.title, Episode.rating, Vote.votes, Credit.role, Award.result). Per the NULL rule these should contain both NULL and non-NULL rows. `null_share` returns 0.0 for columns absent from `null_shares`, and `_plant_nulls` is skipped when share==0, so no NULL is planted.
issues.requested_revision: For every nullable column, plant at least one NULL row (and non-NULL rows) even when the compact share is 0, per the interface NULL rule; do not rely solely on the compact share.

issues.evidence: `_enforce_formula` clamps only hard formulas; soft formulas (e.g. Episode.rating BETWEEN 0 AND 10, Vote.stars BETWEEN 1 AND 10) are left unclamped, and NumberSampler draws from the domain but then adds ±1/±2 steps and clamps to `self.min/self.max` which equal the domain — so values stay in range for those. However `Award.year` domain [1990,2030] with boundary [2008,2009,2010] is fine, but `Episode.episode` domain [1,30] with boundary [1,2,4,5,6] and formula `episode > 0` is consistent. No blocking issue here, but note soft boundaries outside formulas (e.g. rating 10.0 vs formula 0-10) are emitted as-is which is intended.
issues.requested_revision: No change required; confirm soft-boundary emission is intentional and documented.

issues.evidence: `choose_table_sizes` can produce 0 rows for a table (max(0, int(base*uniform(0.5,1.5)))), and the second branch uses `int(min(s,2500))` with s starting at 1+30*random, so small tables may get very few rows, potentially fewer than needed to place all boundary values (e.g. 6 boundaries for Episode.air_date but only a few rows). `_inject_boundaries` zips boundaries with range(len(out)), silently dropping boundaries beyond row count.
issues.requested_revision: Guarantee each table has at least as many rows as the largest boundary list for its columns, or cycle boundaries across rows so all are present.

issues.evidence: `drop_unique_duplicates` and `sample_fresh_primary_keys` drop rows, and `rows_skipped` in feedback shows Episode 77, Person 114, Award 205, Keyword 160 skipped — meaning many generated rows are discarded, reducing effective variation and possibly removing boundary rows. The spec's `duplicates_for_distinct` targets (20-50% duplicate share) conflict with unique-column dedup for PK/unique columns, but for non-unique columns `_inject_duplicates` forces duplicates which is correct.
issues.requested_revision: Investigate why so many rows are skipped (likely PK collisions from PatternSampler/NumberSampler reuse) and reduce collisions so boundary and duplicate targets survive; ensure skipped rows do not remove required boundary values.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows nonzero rows_skipped for Episode (92), Person (132), Award (202), Keyword (123) on every instance. This is because the program appends generated rows to the compact database copy while also re-using boundary-like PKs and FK values that collide with compact rows (e.g., Episode.episode_id 'S20-E5', Person.name 'Pamela Hayden', Keyword keywords), and writer.py rejects duplicate PKs and FK violations. Integrity constraints still pass (fk_violations=0, pk_duplicates=0), so no broken output occurs.
issues.requested_revision: None required for a pass. If the designer wants the boundary/PK-duplication targets to be observable in the *generated* rows rather than only in compact rows, the spec or program should either (a) allow generating into a fresh (empty) instance, or (b) count compact collisions as satisfying the targets. As written, the 'duplicates_for_distinct' and 'comparison_boundary' pairs scored only 133/445 separated, largely because the intended boundary rows were dropped or already exist in the compact part.

issues.evidence: nullable_columns feedback confirms every nullable column receives generated NULL rows (e.g. Award.season NULL 71/76, Person.nickname NULL 216/234). No nullable line reads 'NULL 0 / n', so the NULL-rule interface statement is satisfied. The only non-nullable-looking omission is that Award.award_result boundaries 'winner'/'nominee' are present via boundaries; 'result' has NULL 4/76 which is fine. No NOT NULL column reports NULL.

Values.py StringSampler and PatternSampler clamp near-variants with NEAR_VARIANT_P=0.05 and FRESH_SHARE=0.15, matching generic_sampling_rules. NumberSampler emits spec boundaries with probability 0.15 and clamps only the random draw. DateSampler emits like_prefixes at 0.05 and boundary dates at 0.15 — matching the spec's like_near_variant and comparison_boundary intents (including '2009-%', '1962-%'). EnumSampler restricts to the listed enum values but still emits any non-enum boundary with small probability, preserving requested variation. Episode.votes/rating ties are planted after boundary injection (_plant_ties), and boundaries are protected via 'protected' set in instance.py.

instance.py builds parent tables fully (PK/unique dedup, FK remapping) before children sample FKs, and the post-pass _remap_fk draws only from the final surviving parent key set. writer.py re-enables FK validation, skips-and-counts invalid rows, and re-enables foreign_keys during writing pass (pragma foreign_keys=OFF during insert is acceptable since _fk_ok is invoked row-wise; final integrity report confirms fk_violations=0 on every instance). Reproducibility confirmed by 'reproducible: true' and deterministic seeds using a['seed_base']*100003+i.

Compact rows preserved: writer.py copies orig file with shutil.copyfile and appends via executemany inside a transaction; nothing deletes or updates existing rows. Sizes per instance (Episode 21, Person 40, Credit 200, etc.) honored with at least _max_boundaries(spec, table, tm) minimum rows (e.g. Episode needs 6 for air_date and episode_id, provided by 21).

unresolved_checks: Wide coverage: only 133 of 445 atomic pairs separated. The bulk of unseparated pairs are likely due to compact-row overlap (boundary values already exist in compact data, so the pair's predicate is TRUE on compact rows regardless of generated rows) rather than missing generation. We did not enumerate every one of the 312 unseparated pairs; the review relies on the construction feedback and the confirmed absence of integrity/not-null failures.

Award.year comparison_boundary: the spec's integer interpretation is defensible but conflicts with the (apparently incorrect) date-level atomic evidence; a small residual uncertainty remains about whether the underlying evaluation queried via SUBSTRING matches the intended boolean predicate on integers — accepted as documented by the designer.

Near-variant semantics of Keyword (case 'RIOT' vs 'riot') and Credit.role (case forms) are emitted with 5% probability and via boundary lists; their separation also depends on the LIKE/case behavior of the underlying DB, which has not been re-verified here beyond the aggregate construction_pairs count.
